title: Nutrient Pollution
content: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus entering water bodies can cause excessive algal growth. Nutrient pollution can harm aquatic ecosystems and contribute to harmful algal blooms.

title: Dead Zones and Harmful Algal Blooms
content: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus can cause rapid algal growth. When algae die and decompose, oxygen in the water can be consumed, creating low-oxygen conditions that can make it difficult for aquatic life to survive.

title: Dissolved Oxygen
content: Dissolved oxygen is an important indicator of whether water can support aquatic life. Low dissolved oxygen can stress aquatic organisms, and prolonged very low oxygen can result in mortality.

title: Dissolved Oxygen and Water
content: Dissolved oxygen is needed by aquatic organisms. Warm water generally holds less dissolved oxygen than cold water. Excess organic material and decomposition can also consume oxygen.

title: Phosphorus Indicator
content: Excess phosphorus can contribute to freshwater algal blooms. Excess algal growth can reduce dissolved oxygen, block sunlight and degrade aquatic habitat.

title: Nitrogen Indicator
content: Increased nitrogen inputs can stimulate excessive algal growth. Excess algae can contribute to low dissolved oxygen, harmful algal toxins and degraded aquatic habitat.

title: Dissolved Oxygen Stressors
content: High water temperature can reduce oxygen solubility. High nutrient levels can increase plant and algal growth, and respiration and decomposition can contribute to dissolved oxygen declines.
